item.title: Re: This could be repurposed now
item.content:encoded: General note, authors are free to keep their works as discrete as they like. Just because one author wrote an SCP article with a numerical designation previously only used in a tale, does not mean either author is obligated to combine their works. If the pieces were not written with each other in mind, there's no need to change both to shoehorn in material from each other.

item.title: This could be repurposed now
item.content:encoded: With the creation of SCP-5128 and the new SCP-000, this creature in the empty void could be the "theoretical source of all anomalous behavior" described in those new SCPs. The ripples of energy could be anomalous objects being created (though I can see they may actually be the tickets that Rosen talks of) and the abominations being spoken of could be the people who come into contact with SCP-000 and suffer the infohazardous effect. The being that said "Foundation" could even be D. Cindi van Veenen.

item.content:encoded: Little bit of a necropost here, but the black shapeless entity probably was SCP-S and was not the first entity SCP-000 saw. item.title: Re: Ok so i have a theory about what this is
item.content:encoded:
Given that this is a database-muddling entry, I think it makes sense. In computer programming, everything starts counting from 0, with 1 holding no real significance. It pleases me in a very strange, very nerdy way that this "technical error", numbered zero, could be considered the "first SCP".

I don't agree with the headcanon because the database wouldn't exist without some scips already existing, but it's got some nice symmetry to it.
